spec_text_or_path: Animate Weapon's identity is that weapons/blades LYING ON THE GROUND are the summon ammunition — the loot drop-stream IS the resource pool. Bladefall seeds lingering blade-entities; Animate Weapon consumes those ground entities to spawn transient minions. Engine proxy summoning draws from mana/corpses (resource_economy + PROXY family), NOT from consumed ground-item entities on the floor. No engine lane represents 'ground item entities as a consumable summon resource whose supply is the loot-drop rate'. Mapped as a standard transient poison-proxy swarm (PROXY_FISSION) which loses the loot-becomes-ammo substrate. Would require either (a) a ground-entity-consumption resource primitive, or (b) an explicit ruling that the substrate is flavor-only and the proxy-swarm approximation is canonical.

mechanism_class: role-scope gap: ally-buff-projection (party-support) in a solo-only engine
spec_text_or_path: Aurabot's entire purpose is reserving the full pool to project 10-16 auras onto ALLIES (Generosity shares to allies, NOT self), multiplying PARTY output with zero personal damage — explicitly 'useless solo' (source mech_note). The engine is solo-scope; there is no ally to receive the projected buff, so the kit's reason-for-existing has no lane. This is NOT a missing mechanism minted by adding a mechanic — it is a fundamental scope boundary (solo vs party). Distinct from aurastacker (self-recipient, IS solo-viable). SECONDARY tension shared with aurastacker: source reserves ~100% of pool, exceeding the engine reservation_percent 0.75 LOCKED cap (clamped in-map). Destination is the docket as a scope-boundary record: either (a) Aurabot is permanently out-of-scope (party-support has no solo home), or (b) a future co-op/party layer would re-home it. No author mint is appropriate against a scope boundary.
